## Purpose

This note consolidates the Chen and Yang (2019) application into one main document.
The goals are:

- summarize the experiment and the original Table 3 analysis;
- reproduce the paper's benchmark reduced-form estimates;
- re-run the main contrasts using the updated `riattrition` package;
- visualize how attrition changes the randomization distribution; and
- bring the main attrition diagnostics into a single workflow.

## Summary of the Experiment

### Substantive question

Chen and Yang (2019) study whether access to uncensored information changes what
Chinese university students know, believe, and intend to do politically. The
paper focuses on the effects of media censorship by experimentally varying
access to foreign news websites that are blocked by the Great Firewall.

### Treatment arms

The experiment includes four relevant arms:

- `Control`: no new access and no newsletter encouragement.
- `A` (Access only): students receive free VPN access but no direct encouragement to consume blocked foreign news.
- `CE` (Encouragement only): students receive newsletters encouraging foreign news consumption, but no VPN access.
- `AE` (Access plus encouragement): students receive both VPN access and newsletter encouragement.

The contrast structure in Table 3 therefore centers on three two-arm
comparisons:

- `AE` versus `Control`
- `A` versus `Control`
- `CE` versus `Control`

### Outcomes

Table 3 reports reduced-form treatment effects for five standardized wave-3
outcome families:

1. media-related behaviors
2. knowledge
3. economic beliefs
4. political attitudes
5. behaviors and planned behaviors

### Attrition in the paper

The paper's main Table 3 analysis is a wave-3 respondent analysis. In other
words, the published regression results condition on being observed at endline.
The paper argues that attrition is unlikely to create serious bias because:

- attrition does not differ significantly across treatment arms;
- baseline and endline samples look similar on observables; and
- baseline outcomes do not strongly predict later attrition.

These are exactly the kinds of claims we want to revisit using the updated
package and a more explicit missingness framework.

## Application Strategy

The updated package is designed around binary contrasts. That fits this
application well because Chen and Yang's Table 3 already emphasizes three binary
treatment-versus-control comparisons.

The plan is:

1. reproduce the paper's benchmark reduced-form estimates using the wave-3
   respondent sample and the paper's restriction that drops prior VPN users;
2. move to the full contrast sample, still dropping prior VPN users, and apply
   `ri_sharp_attrition()` outcome by outcome;
3. compare `general` missingness to a one-sided monotone assumption selected by
   the observed attrition imbalance; and
4. visualize the media outcome across all three contrasts using `plot_ri_test_stat()`.

The package application treats each of the three Table 3 comparisons as a
complete-randomization binary experiment.

## Reusable Local Helpers

The helpers below are not part of the package. They are only document-side
convenience wrappers for repetitive tasks such as:

- constructing the three binary contrasts;
- looping over the five Table 3 outcomes; and
- collecting selected fields from repeated package calls into compact tables.

The actual inference in this note still comes from the package functions
`ri_sharp_attrition()` and `plot_ri_test_stat()`.

```{r}
make_contrast <- function(dat, treat_var) {
  dat %>%
    filter(Z_treatment_control == 1 | .data[[treat_var]] == 1) %>%
    mutate(Z = ifelse(.data[[treat_var]] == 1, 1L, 0L))
}

choose_monotone_assumption <- function(Y, Z) {
  p_obs_treat <- mean(!is.na(Y[Z == 1]))
  p_obs_control <- mean(!is.na(Y[Z == 0]))
  if (p_obs_treat >= p_obs_control) "mp" else "mn"
}

extract_assumption_row <- function(out, assumption) {
  assumption_col <- if ("Assumption" %in% names(out$results)) {
    "Assumption"
  } else {
    "Missingness assumption"
  }
  idx <- which(out$results[[assumption_col]] == assumption)
  if (length(idx) == 0) return(NULL)
  out$results[idx, , drop = FALSE]
}

extract_result_value <- function(row, candidates) {
  hit <- intersect(candidates, names(row))
  if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA)
  row[[hit[1]]][1]
}

format_result_ci <- function(row) {
  if (is.null(row)) return(NA_character_)

  if ("[95% C.I.]" %in% names(row)) {
    return(row$`[95% C.I.]`[1])
  }

  if (all(c("CI lower", "CI upper") %in% names(row))) {
    lower <- row$`CI lower`[1]
    upper <- row$`CI upper`[1]
    return(sprintf("[%s, %s]", format(lower, trim = TRUE), format(upper, trim = TRUE)))
  }

  NA_character_
}

format_est_se <- function(model, term) {
  ct <- coeftable(model)
  if (!(term %in% rownames(ct))) return("")
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", ct[term, "Estimate"], ct[term, "Std. Error"])
}

format_term_label <- function(term) {
  if (term == "(Intercept)") return("Constant")
  if (term == "Z") return("Treatment")
  if (grepl("^Z:", term)) return(sub("^Z:", "Treatment × ", term))
  term
}

wald_p_selected <- function(model, terms) {
  b <- coef(model)
  V <- vcov(model)
  idx <- match(terms, names(b))
  idx <- idx[!is.na(idx)]

  if (length(idx) == 0) return(NA_real_)

  R <- diag(length(b))[idx, , drop = FALSE]
  RVRT <- R %*% V %*% t(R)

  if (qr(RVRT)$rank < nrow(RVRT)) return(NA_real_)

  W <- as.numeric(t(R %*% b) %*% solve(RVRT) %*% (R %*% b))
  1 - pchisq(W, df = nrow(R))
}

run_original_rf <- function(dat, y_vars) {
  lapply(y_vars, function(y) {
    model <- feols(as.formula(paste0(y, " ~ Z")), data = dat, vcov = "HC1")
    ct <- coeftable(model)
    tibble(
      outcome = y,
      estimate = unname(ct["Z", "Estimate"]),
      se = unname(ct["Z", "Std. Error"]),
      p_value = unname(ct["Z", "Pr(>|t|)"])
    )
  }) %>% bind_rows()
}

run_package_application <- function(dat, y_vars, nperm = 10000) {
  map_dfr(seq_along(y_vars), function(i) {
    y <- y_vars[i]
    set.seed(20260514 + i - 1)
    mono_assumption <- choose_monotone_assumption(dat[[y]], dat$Z)
    out <- ri_sharp_attrition(
      Z = dat$Z,
      Y = dat[[y]],
      c = 0,
      missing = mono_assumption,
      class = "RS",
      method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
      nperm = nperm,
      include_twostep = FALSE
    )

    general_row <- extract_assumption_row(out, "general")
    mono_row <- extract_assumption_row(out, mono_assumption)

    tibble(
      outcome = y,
      mono_assumption = mono_assumption,
      n_total = out$counts$n_total,
      n_missing = out$counts$n_miss,
      attrition_rate = out$counts$attrition_rate_total,
      p_obs_treat = out$counts$n_obs_treat / out$counts$n_treat,
      p_obs_control = out$counts$n_obs_control / out$counts$n_control,
      general_value = extract_result_value(general_row, c("Value", "Test stat. value")),
      general_p = extract_result_value(general_row, c("P-value")),
      general_ci = format_result_ci(general_row),
      mono_value = extract_result_value(mono_row, c("Value", "Test stat. value")),
      mono_p = extract_result_value(mono_row, c("P-value")),
      mono_ci = format_result_ci(mono_row)
    )
  })
}

run_group_observability_table <- function(dat, covariates, m_var = "panelmerged_wave3") {
  fit_group <- function(z_value) {
    dd <- dat %>%
      mutate(M = as.integer(.data[[m_var]] == 1)) %>%
      filter(Z == z_value) %>%
      select(M, all_of(covariates)) %>%
      na.omit()

    model <- feols(
      as.formula(paste0("M ~ ", paste(covariates, collapse = " + "))),
      data = dd,
      vcov = "HC1"
    )

    list(model = model, n = nobs(model))
  }

  control_fit <- fit_group(0)
  treat_fit <- fit_group(1)

  tibble(term = covariates) %>%
    mutate(
      term_label = vapply(term, format_term_label, character(1)),
      control_group = vapply(term, function(x) format_est_se(control_fit$model, x), character(1)),
      treatment_group = vapply(term, function(x) format_est_se(treat_fit$model, x), character(1))
    ) %>%
    select(term_label, control_group, treatment_group) %>%
    bind_rows(
      tibble(
        term_label = "Constant",
        control_group = format_est_se(control_fit$model, "(Intercept)"),
        treatment_group = format_est_se(treat_fit$model, "(Intercept)")
      ),
      tibble(
        term_label = "N",
        control_group = as.character(control_fit$n),
        treatment_group = as.character(treat_fit$n)
      )
    )
}

run_missingness_regression_pair <- function(dat, covariates, m_var = "panelmerged_wave3") {
  dd <- dat %>%
    mutate(M = as.integer(.data[[m_var]] == 1)) %>%
    select(M, Z, all_of(covariates)) %>%
    na.omit()

  model_a <- feols(
    as.formula(paste0("M ~ ", paste(covariates, collapse = " + "))),
    data = dd,
    vcov = "HC1"
  )

  model_b <- feols(
    as.formula(paste0("M ~ Z * (", paste(covariates, collapse = " + "), ")")),
    data = dd,
    vcov = "HC1"
  )

  terms_b <- c(covariates, "Z", paste0("Z:", covariates))
  table_df <- tibble(term = c(covariates, "Z", paste0("Z:", covariates))) %>%
    mutate(
      term_label = vapply(term, format_term_label, character(1)),
      reg_a = vapply(term, function(x) format_est_se(model_a, x), character(1)),
      reg_b = vapply(term, function(x) format_est_se(model_b, x), character(1))
    ) %>%
    select(term_label, reg_a, reg_b) %>%
    bind_rows(
      tibble(
        term_label = "Constant",
        reg_a = format_est_se(model_a, "(Intercept)"),
        reg_b = format_est_se(model_b, "(Intercept)")
      ),
      tibble(
        term_label = "N",
        reg_a = as.character(nobs(model_a)),
        reg_b = as.character(nobs(model_b))
      )
    )

  list(
    table = table_df,
    p_all_x = wald_p_selected(model_a, covariates),
    p_all_xz = wald_p_selected(model_b, paste0("Z:", covariates))
  )
}
```

## Define Analysis Samples

```{r}
chen_table3 <- chen_yang %>%
  filter(panelmerged_wave3 == 1) %>%
  filter(D_prior_vpn_user != 1)

chen_full <- chen_yang %>%
  filter(D_prior_vpn_user != 1)

contrast_AE_table3 <- make_contrast(chen_table3, "Z_treatment_vpnnl")
contrast_A_table3 <- make_contrast(chen_table3, "Z_treatment_vpnonly")
contrast_CE_table3 <- make_contrast(chen_table3, "Z_treatment_nlonly")

contrast_AE_full <- make_contrast(chen_full, "Z_treatment_vpnnl")
contrast_A_full <- make_contrast(chen_full, "Z_treatment_vpnonly")
contrast_CE_full <- make_contrast(chen_full, "Z_treatment_nlonly")

contrast_sizes <- tibble(
  contrast = c("AE vs Control", "A vs Control", "CE vs Control"),
  n_table3 = c(nrow(contrast_AE_table3), nrow(contrast_A_table3), nrow(contrast_CE_table3)),
  n_full = c(nrow(contrast_AE_full), nrow(contrast_A_full), nrow(contrast_CE_full))
)

kable(contrast_sizes, digits = 0)
```

## Reproducing the Original Table 3 Benchmarks

This section uses the paper's wave-3 respondent sample and drops prior VPN users.
It therefore mirrors the conventional complete-case logic in the published table.

```{r}
rf_AE <- run_original_rf(contrast_AE_table3, outcomes) %>% mutate(contrast = "AE vs Control")
rf_A <- run_original_rf(contrast_A_table3, outcomes) %>% mutate(contrast = "A vs Control")
rf_CE <- run_original_rf(contrast_CE_table3, outcomes) %>% mutate(contrast = "CE vs Control")

rf_all <- bind_rows(rf_AE, rf_A, rf_CE) %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome]) %>%
  select(contrast, outcome_label, estimate, se, p_value)

kable(rf_all, digits = 3)
```

## Applying `ri_sharp_attrition()`

This section moves to the full contrast sample, still excluding prior VPN users,
and applies the updated package outcome by outcome. For each outcome:

- `general` is always reported;
- a one-sided monotone restriction is chosen from the observed arm-specific
  observability rates; and
- the package prints the corresponding finite-sample RI summaries.

### AE vs Control

```{r}
set.seed(20260514)
ae_media_direct <- ri_sharp_attrition(
  Z = contrast_AE_full$Z,
  Y = contrast_AE_full$Y_az_overall_a_w3,
  c = 0,
  missing = choose_monotone_assumption(
    contrast_AE_full$Y_az_overall_a_w3,
    contrast_AE_full$Z
  ),
  class = "RS",
  method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
  nperm = 10000,
  include_twostep = FALSE
)

ae_media_direct
```

```{r}
ae_results <- run_package_application(contrast_AE_full, outcomes, nperm = 10000) %>%
  mutate(contrast = "AE vs Control", outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome]) %>%
  select(contrast, outcome_label, mono_assumption, attrition_rate,
         p_obs_treat, p_obs_control, general_p, general_ci, mono_p, mono_ci)

kable(ae_results, digits = 3)
```

## Visualizing Inference

This section uses the media outcome for all three contrasts so that
`general`, `mp`, and `complete-case` inference can be compared directly.

### AE vs Control: general missingness

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
set.seed(11215)
ae_media_general_plot <- plot_ri_test_stat(
  Z = contrast_AE_full$Z,
  Y = contrast_AE_full$Y_az_overall_a_w3,
  c = 0,
  missing = "general",
  class = "RS",
  method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
  nperm = 10000
)
```

### AE vs Control: monotone positive missingness

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
set.seed(11215)
ae_media_mp_plot <- plot_ri_test_stat(
  Z = contrast_AE_full$Z,
  Y = contrast_AE_full$Y_az_overall_a_w3,
  c = 0,
  analysis = "mp",
  missing = "mp",
  class = "RS",
  method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
  nperm = 10000
)
```

### AE vs Control: complete-case analysis

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
set.seed(11215)
ae_media_complete_plot <- plot_ri_test_stat(
  Z = contrast_AE_full$Z,
  Y = contrast_AE_full$Y_az_overall_a_w3,
  c = 0,
  analysis = "complete-case",
  class = "RS",
  method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
  nperm = 10000
)
```

```{r}

  class = "RS",
  method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
  nperm = 10000
)
```

### CE vs Control: monotone positive missingness

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
set.seed(11215)
ce_media_mp_plot <- plot_ri_test_stat(
  Z = contrast_CE_full$Z,
  Y = contrast_CE_full$Y_az_overall_a_w3,
  c = 0,
  analysis = "mp",
  missing = "mp",
  class = "RS",
  method.list = list(name = "Wilcoxon"),
  nperm = 10000
)
```

set.seed(11215)

## Attrition Diagnostics

### Arm-specific observability

```{r}
diagnostic_overview <- bind_rows(
  ae_results,
  a_results,
  ce_results
) %>%
  select(contrast, outcome_label, attrition_rate, p_obs_treat, p_obs_control, mono_assumption)

kable(diagnostic_overview, digits = 3)
```

The remaining diagnostics use a single outcome-agnostic observability indicator,
`M = 1{ observed at wave 3 }`. In this dataset, that indicator is identical to
the missingness pattern for all five Table 3 outcome families, so it provides a
clean summary of overall attrition.

### Regressions by experimental group

These tables follow the Gerber and Green template by estimating
`M ~ X` separately within the control arm and the treatment arm.

```{r}
ae_group_table <- run_group_observability_table(contrast_AE_full, covars)
a_group_table <- run_group_observability_table(contrast_A_full, covars)
ce_group_table <- run_group_observability_table(contrast_CE_full, covars)

kable(ae_group_table, caption = "AE vs Control", col.names = c("Covariate", "Control group", "Treatment group"))
kable(a_group_table, caption = "A vs Control", col.names = c("Covariate", "Control group", "Treatment group"))
kable(ce_group_table, caption = "CE vs Control", col.names = c("Covariate", "Control group", "Treatment group"))
```

### Missingness regressions with and without interactions

The next tables report:

- regression (a): `M ~ X`
- regression (b): `M ~ X + Z + X * Z`

For each contrast, the footnote reports:

- a joint `p`-value for the null that all `X` coefficients in regression (a)
  equal zero; and
- a joint `p`-value for the null that all interaction coefficients `X * Z` in
  regression (b) equal zero.

```{r}
ae_reg_pair <- run_missingness_regression_pair(contrast_AE_full, covars)
a_reg_pair <- run_missingness_regression_pair(contrast_A_full, covars)
ce_reg_pair <- run_missingness_regression_pair(contrast_CE_full, covars)

kable(
  ae_reg_pair$table,
  caption = paste0(
    "AE vs Control. Footnote: joint p-value for all X in regression (a) = ",
    sprintf("%.3f", ae_reg_pair$p_all_x),
    "; joint p-value for all X × Z in regression (b) = ",
    sprintf("%.3f", ae_reg_pair$p_all_xz),
    "."
  ),
  col.names = c("Term", "(a) M ~ X", "(b) M ~ X + Z + X × Z")
)

kable(
  a_reg_pair$table,
  caption = paste0(
    "A vs Control. Footnote: joint p-value for all X in regression (a) = ",
    sprintf("%.3f", a_reg_pair$p_all_x),
    "; joint p-value for all X × Z in regression (b) = ",
    sprintf("%.3f", a_reg_pair$p_all_xz),
    "."
  ),
  col.names = c("Term", "(a) M ~ X", "(b) M ~ X + Z + X × Z")
)

kable(
  ce_reg_pair$table,
  caption = paste0(
    "CE vs Control. Footnote: joint p-value for all X in regression (a) = ",
    sprintf("%.3f", ce_reg_pair$p_all_x),
    "; joint p-value for all X × Z in regression (b) = ",
    sprintf("%.3f", ce_reg_pair$p_all_xz),
    "."
  ),
  col.names = c("Term", "(a) M ~ X", "(b) M ~ X + Z + X × Z")
)
```
